title: Azure RBAC Scopes and Roles
description: Explore how RBAC scopes work and choose the right built-in or custom role for your scenario.

data.text: Scope in RBAC determines the boundary where a role assignment is effective. Think of it like layers of an onion — the narrower the scope, the more secure your permissions.

data.title: RBAC Scope Hierarchy
items: Management group — applies to multiple subscriptions
Subscription — applies to everything in a subscription
Resource group — applies to one resource group
Resource — applies to a single resource like a storage account

data.title: View All Role Assignments at Subscription Scope
data.content: Use Azure CLI to list every role assignment in a subscription.

data.title: Create a Custom Role with JSON
data.content: Define a custom role that allows reading blobs but not modifying them.
data.code:
{
  "Name": "Blob Reader Only",
  "IsCustom": true,
  "Description": "Read blobs without write access.",
  "Actions": [
    "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/read",
    "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/generateUserDelegationKey/action"
  ],
  "NotActions": [],
  "DataActions": [
    "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/blobs/read"
  ],
  "AssignableScopes": ["/subscriptions/{subscription-id}"]
}

data.text: Role assignments inherit downward and never upward. A role assigned at the subscription applies to every resource group and resource below it; a role assigned at a resource group does not apply to another resource group or to the subscription. This is why the narrowest scope that still works is the safest default.

Changes are not always instantaneous. Role assignments usually take effect within a few minutes, but can take longer because Azure caches authorization decisions. If a newly granted permission does not work, wait and retry before changing the design.

data.title: Create and inspect a custom role
data.content: Custom roles start from a JSON definition with Actions, NotActions, and AssignableScopes. Actions use the provider operation format.
data.code:
# Save the role definition from the previous example as blob-reader.json
az role definition create --role-definition @blob-reader.json

# Confirm the role exists and inspect its permissions
az role definition list --name "Blob Reader Only" -o json

# Assign it at the storage account scope only
az role assignment create \
  --assignee-object-id "$principalId" \
  --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
  --role "Blob Reader Only" \
  --scope "$storageId"

data.title: Choosing a role safely
items: Start with the narrowest built-in role that covers the needed operations; custom roles add maintenance overhead.
Assign at resource or resource group scope for application identities, not at subscription scope.
Use groups for humans and managed identities for workloads, so joiners and leavers are handled in one place.
Review assignments with az role assignment list --all and remove unused ones.
Use PIM (Privileged Identity Management) for just-in-time access to privileged roles instead of permanent Owner.

data.title: Owner is rarely the right answer
data.text: Owner includes the ability to delegate access, which means an identity with Owner can grant itself or anyone else any permission. For application identities, prefer a data-plane role or a narrowly scoped custom role. Reserve Owner and User Access Administrator for break-glass accounts.

data.title: Scope Exploration
data.description: Create a role assignment at the resource group scope, then verify it applies only to resources inside that group.
steps: Assign the Reader role to your user at the resource group scope.
Try to list storage accounts in a different resource group.
data.expectedOutcome: You can read resources in 'scoped-rg' but cannot see resources in other groups.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Scope is hierarchical: management group > subscription > resource group > resource.
Use the narrowest scope that still works.
Custom roles let you fine-tune permissions when built-in roles are too broad.
